title: Mediterranean Diet and Life Expectancy in Ancient Greece
content: Nutrition is an aspect of daily life shaped by economic, social, cultural, and geographical factors. The dietary habits of Greeks have not changed substantially over the centuries and are based on the Mediterranean food triad of oil, wheat, and wine, forming the pillars of the Mediterranean Diet. Adults in ancient Greece, who overcame infancy, often had high life expectancy and many ancient writers and scholars attribute this longevity to their self-control, mental activity and simple eating habits. The purpose of this article is to both put value to the many great effects of the well-known Mediterranean nutrition, as well as to offer insights considering its relation to the longevity (μακροζωία, makrozoia) of the Greeks during ancient times.
